summary: Alasdair MacIntyre (1929–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Epsom College, Queen Mary University of London, and the University of Manchester. He held posts at Essex, Brandeis, Duke, London Metropolitan University, and the University of Notre Dame (~1988–2010).

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (MA) and the University of Pittsburgh (PhD). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Toronto.

Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge. He has held positions at SOAS, the Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel, Ferdinand Sommer, Friedrich Leo, and Alfred Körte. His academic posts included Zurich, Greifswald, Jena, the University of Basel, and the University of Bern.

Albert Grünwedel (1856–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich and served extensively at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, including as director (1904–1921).

Albert Hoefer (1812–1883) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Greifswald, where he served as an außerordentlicher Professor from 1847 to 1880.
Albert Hofmann (1906–2008) studied at the University of Zurich from approximately 1925 to 1929. He later held a post at Novartis from around 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker, later serving at Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art and as director from 1998 to 2019.

Albert Schweitzer (1875–1965) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Wilhelm Deecke and at the universities of Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Prague, later holding a post at the University of Strasbourg from around 1902 to 1912.

Albert Sechehaye (1870–1946) was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva, where he was a student of Ferdinand de Saussure. He subsequently held a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1903 to 1946.

Albert Thumb (1865–1915) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing habilitation at Freiburg. He held posts at the University of Freiburg, the University of Strasbourg, and the University of Marburg.

Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University, studying under Koichi Shinohara, Yun-hua Jan, and Ryosho Tanaka, and held posts at the University of Winnipeg and the University of Arizona.

Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held a post as a guest at the Institute for Research in Humanities at Kyoto University and an affiliation at the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University (PhD), supervised by Robert A. F. Thurman among numerous other academic and traditional teachers.

Albrecht Hanisch works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, and has served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber (1825–1901) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Stenzler, Lassen, Gildemeister, and Kuhn. He served at the Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 to 1901 and was a member of the Prussian Academy.

Albrecht Wezler (1938–2023) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and directed the Nepal Research Centre and Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs and has held posts at Shan State Buddhist University, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

Aleksander Brückner (1856–1939) was a linguist and historian. He studied at the University of Lviv, the University of Vienna, and Frederick William University Berlin under August Leskien, subsequently holding academic posts at Lviv (~1878–1881) and Berlin (~1881–1924).
Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist and linguist. He holds a post at the University of Munich and serves as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
